title: The Largest Value in a Subtree, With Changes

concept.title: After numbering the nodes in a depth-first order, the subtree of a node is a range of positions, and a segment tree answers its maximum
body: A rooted tree has a number in every node. An operation **replaces the value of a node**, and a question asks for the **largest value in the subtree of a node** (the node itself and all its descendants). For the tree with the root 1 and its children 2 and 3, with the values `4, 9, 2`, the largest value in the subtree of the root is 9, and in the subtree of the node 3 it is 2. Collecting the values of a subtree for every question costs O(size of the subtree).

Number the nodes in the order of a depth-first walk (the *Euler tour*). Then the subtree of `v` occupies the **consecutive positions** `tin[v] .. tin[v] + size[v] - 1`. The question turns into "what is the largest number in this range of positions?", which a segment tree answers in O(log n), and a change of a node value is a change of one cell at the position `tin[v]`. The numbering needs no recursion here, because the parent of every node has a smaller number: the sizes are collected from the last node to the first, and the positions are handed out from the first node to the last.

body.code:
size[v] = 1 + the sizes of its children      # add each node to its parent, last node first
tin[1] = 0; nxt[1] = 1
for v in 2 .. n:
    tin[v] = nxt[parent[v]]; nxt[parent[v]] += size[v]; nxt[v] = tin[v] + 1
leaf[tin[v]] = value[v]
# change:    set the leaf at tin[v]
# question:  the maximum over the positions tin[v] .. tin[v] + size[v] - 1

body: Each operation costs O(log n). The same numbering supports "sum of a subtree", "add to a subtree" and "count nodes with a property in a subtree" with the matching structure (a Fenwick or a segment tree) over the positions.

statement: A rooted tree with `n` nodes (the root is the node 1, and the parent of every node has a smaller number) has a value in every node. Process `q` operations: type 1 `v x` sets the value of the node `v` to `x`; type 2 `v 0` asks for the largest value among the node `v` and all its descendants. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of nodes and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the parent of every node (0 for the root, which is the node 1; the parent of a node has a smaller number).
The third line has `n` numbers: the values of the nodes.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `v` and `x`. If `t = 1`, set the value of the node `v` to `x`. If `t = 2`, print the largest value in the subtree of the node `v` (`x` is 0).
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.

examples.note: The largest value in the whole tree is 9, and in the subtree of the node 3 it is 2: 9 2.

hints: Number the nodes in depth-first order so that every subtree is a range.
Compute the sizes from the last node to the first, since parents have smaller numbers.
Use a maximum segment tree over the positions.

explanation: The nodes are numbered in depth-first order so that every subtree is a range of positions; a maximum segment tree over these positions answers the largest value of a subtree and supports changing a node.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
par = list(map(int, input().split()))
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

sz = [1] * (n + 1)
for v in range(n, 1, -1):
    sz[par[v - 1]] += sz[v]
tin = [0] * (n + 1)
nxt = [0] * (n + 1)
nxt[1] = 1
for v in range(2, n + 1):
    p = par[v - 1]
    tin[v] = nxt[p]
    nxt[p] += sz[v]
    nxt[v] = tin[v] + 1
size = 1
while size < n:
    size *= 2
low = -(1 << 62)
tree = [low] * (2 * size)
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    tree[size + tin[v]] = a[v - 1]
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
    tree[v] = max(tree[2 * v], tree[2 * v + 1])
out = []
for kind, v, x in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        u = size + tin[v]
        tree[u] = x
        u //= 2
        while u:
            tree[u] = max(tree[2 * u], tree[2 * u + 1])
            u //= 2
    else:
        lo = size + tin[v]
        hi = lo + sz[v]
        res = low
        while lo < hi:
            if lo & 1:
                res = max(res, tree[lo])
                lo += 1
            if hi & 1:
                hi -= 1
                res = max(res, tree[hi])
            lo //= 2
            hi //= 2
        out.append(res)
print(*out)
